codeReview.summary: The rerun fixes the prior underflow panic path for small fixtures, but the new implementation still fails parity for `--max-count=0` by treating 0 as a hard 10,000 cap instead of unlimited behavior, so the feature remains blocking.

issues.description: `Opts::parse()` normalizes `--max-count=0` to `DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT` (10,000), which diverges from ag semantics where 0 means unlimited. This still breaks `--nomultiline -m0 -v` on high-match files: with a 12,050-line all-match file, `./ag --nocolor --nomultiline -m0 -v NEEDLE /tmp/max0_all_match.txt` exits 1 with empty stdout/stderr, but `cargo run -q -p rust-ag -- --nocolor --nomultiline -m0 -v NEEDLE /tmp/max0_all_match.txt` exits 0, prints 2,050 lines, and emits `ERR: Too many matches...` due to the 10,000 cutoff.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Baseline max-count semantics are easy to misread because help text and implementation differ; this should be captured in shared library notes for parity work.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `src/options.c:97` says max-count default is 10,000, but `src/options.c:157` initializes `opts.max_matches_per_file = 0` and `src/search.c:109`/`132`/`164` gate truncation behind `opts.max_matches_per_file > 0`, making 0 effectively unlimited.
